title: Insights into dietary phytochemicals targeting Parkinson's disease key genes and pathways: A network pharmacology approach.
authors: Sasikumar, Devi Soorya Narayana; Thiruselvam, Premkumar; Sundararajan, Vino; Ravindran, Radhika; Gunasekaran, Shoba; Madathil, Deepa; Kaliamurthi, Satyavani; Peslherbe, Gilles H; Selvaraj, Gurudeeban; Sudhakaran, Sajitha Lulu
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络药理学和分子动力学研究膳食植物化学物靶向帕金森病关键基因，虽涉及转录因子和MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a complex neurological disease associated with the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons. Oxidative stress is a key player in instigating apoptosis in dopaminergic neurons. To improve the survival of neurons many dietary phytochemicals have gathered significant attention recently. Thus, the present study implements a comprehensive network pharmacology approach to unravel the mechanisms of action of dietary phytochemicals that benefit disease management. A literature search was performed to identify ligands (i.e., comprising dietary phytochemicals and Food and Drug Administration pre-approved PD drugs) in the PubMed database. Targets associated with selected ligands were extracted from the search tool for interactions of chemicals (STITCH) database. Then, the construction of a gene-gene interaction (GGI) network, analysis of hub-gene, functional and pathway enrichment, associated transcription factors, miRNAs, ligand-target interaction network, docking were performed using various bioinformatics tools together with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The database search resulted in 69 ligands and 144 unique targets. GGI and subsequent topological measures indicate histone acetyltransferase p300 (EP300), mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (MAPK1) or extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK)2, and CREB-binding protein (CREBBP) as hub genes. Neurodegeneration, MAPK signaling, apoptosis, and zinc binding are key pathways and gene ontology terms. hsa-miR-5692a and SCNA gene-associated transcription factors interact with all the 3 hub genes. Ligand-target interaction (LTI) network analysis suggest rasagiline and baicalein as candidate ligands targeting MAPK1. Rasagiline and baicalein form stable complexes with the Y205, K330, and V173 residues of MAPK1. Computational molecular insights suggest that baicalein and rasagiline are promising preclinical candidates for PD management.
abstract_zh: 帕金森病（Parkinson's disease, PD）是一种与多巴胺能神经元退化相关的复杂神经系统疾病。氧化应激是引发多巴胺能神经元凋亡的关键因素。为改善神经元存活，近年来许多膳食植物化学物质引起了广泛关注。因此，本研究采用综合网络药理学方法，以揭示有益于疾病管理的膳食植物化学物质的作用机制。在PubMed数据库中进行文献检索，以识别配体（即包含膳食植物化学物质及美国食品药品监督管理局预批准的PD药物）。从化学物质相互作用搜索工具（STITCH）数据库中提取与选定配体相关的靶点。随后，利用多种生物信息学工具结合分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）模拟，进行了基因-基因相互作用（GGI）网络的构建、枢纽基因分析、功能与通路富集、相关转录因子、miRNA、配体-靶点相互作用网络及对接分析。数据库检索共获得69个配体和144个独特靶点。GGI及后续拓扑测量表明，组蛋白乙酰转移酶p300（EP300）、丝裂原活化蛋白激酶1（MAPK1）或细胞外信号调节激酶（ERK）2，以及CREB结合蛋白（CREBBP）为枢纽基因。神经退行性变、MAPK信号传导、凋亡和锌结合是关键通路及基因本体论条目。hsa-miR-5692a和SCNA基因相关转录因子与所有3个枢纽基因相互作用。配体-靶点相互作用（LTI）网络分析提示，雷沙吉兰和黄芩素为靶向MAPK1的候选配体。雷沙吉兰和黄芩素与MAPK1的Y205、K330和V173残基形成稳定复合物。计算分子见解表明，黄芩素和雷沙吉兰是PD管理的潜在临床前候选药物。
